content_preview.title: Supreme Court Agrees to Hear Apple's Appeal of Epic Games App Store Contempt Ruling
content_preview.summary: The justices granted certiorari limited to whether Apple's App Store fees violated the "spirit" of a 2021 injunction, setting up arguments in the term beginning October 2026.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

The Supreme Court agreed on June 30, 2026, to hear Apple's appeal of a civil contempt finding in its long-running antitrust dispute with Epic Games over App Store payment rules, according to [9to5Mac](https://9to5mac.com/2026/06/30/supreme-court-agrees-to-hear-apple-appeal-over-epic-games-ruling/). The justices granted certiorari "limited to Question 1 presented by the petition," according to [SCOTUSblog](https://www.scotusblog.com/cases/apple-inc-v-epic-games-inc-2/) — the question...

editor_notes.content_quality: Well-structured News piece (565 words, within the 400-1200 range) using the site's standard Overview / What We Know / sub-headed timeline / Reactions / What We Don't Know format. Prose is clear, neutral, and appropriately hedges on unresolved questions (exact argument date, downstream effect on Apple's current fee arrangement).
editor_notes.source_verification: Personally decompressed and read all 4 gzipped snapshots in sources/2026-07/supreme-court-agrees-to-hear-apples-appeal-of-epic-games-app-store-contempt-ruling/ (sha256 of each recomputed and matched against manifest.json, confirming snapshot integrity). source-0.html.gz (MacRumors, Juli Clover, June 30 2026): confirms cert grant, Apple statement, Judge Gonzalez Rogers' 2021 order, the 12-27% vs 15-30% fee figures (verbatim), the October term start, and Apple's 'clear and unambiguous violation' framing. source-1.html.gz (9to5Mac, Ryan Christoffel, June 30 2026): confirms the cert grant, the Bloomberg (Leah Nylen) quote about the justices reviewing 'willfully defied a 2021 ruling,' the Court declining Apple's second question on the 'universal injunction,' the verbatim Apple spokesperson statement, and the verbatim Epic Games X post. source-2.html.gz (SCOTUSblog, docket 25-1311): confirms the docket number, term (October Term 2026), and the Question 1 text reproduced verbatim in the article, including 'Petition GRANTED limited to Question 1 presented by the petition.' source-3.html.gz (PYMNTS, June 30 2026): confirms the 2020 origin of the dispute and the 'external payments...bypass the fees' phrasing (verbatim), the October term timing, and independently corroborates the Question 1 text via its Ars Technica citation. All 4 sources returned HTTP 200 with no archive_fallback. Every direct quote in the article was checked word-for-word against its cited snapshot and matches.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: No fabricated or unsourced specifics found. Every number (docket No. 25-1311, the 12-27% vs 15-30% fee range, the October 2026 term start), name (Judge Yvonne Gonzalez Rogers), and quote traces to a cited source. Internal links to the site's prior April 2026 and May 2026 coverage of this case were cross-checked against those published articles' text (April 2025 willful contempt finding, December 2025 Ninth Circuit 'reasonable fee' ruling) and are consistent — no contradictions in the ongoing story's timeline.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral throughout; both Apple's and Epic's statements are quoted in full and given equal weight. The automated 'loaded language' finding (matching the word 'clearly') was investigated and is a false positive: the word appears only inside a verbatim, quote-marked reproduction of the Supreme Court's own Question 1 text, not as editorializing by the bot. No tone concerns.
editor_notes.originality: Not a duplicate. This is a new, discrete development (cert granted June 30, 2026) in a story the site has followed since April 2026 (petition filed) and May 2026 (stay denied / cert petition filed). Checked src/content/articles/2026-06/ and src/content/articles/2026-07/ for overlap; the only other recent Apple/App-Store Supreme Court coverage is the unrelated Texas age-verification case (2026-07-13) and the EU DMA gatekeeper ruling (2026-07-14), neither of which covers the Epic Games contempt appeal.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Clean, well-sourced submission. All four sources were fetched successfully, personally read, and every claim, number, and quote in the article traces verbatim to a cited source. The sole automated finding ('loaded language': clearly) is a false positive arising from a verbatim quotation of the Court's own certiorari question and does not warrant a corrections record. Verdict: APPROVE.
